recognize_zh: 周邊血液中左下方一顆偏藍紫色的紅血球及右側重疊紅血球內，可見多顆深藍色粗點狀顆粒（粗嗜鹼性點彩），其餘紅血球多為正常大小，配合病史提示鉛中毒。
features: A few red cells with coarse dark-blue cytoplasmic dots (coarse basophilic stippling)
Stippled cells show a faint polychromatic, bluish-gray tint; one polychromatic cell without clear stippling nearby
Majority of red cells normocytic and normochromic with central pallor
Occasional crenated red cells and small fragments
Scattered normal platelets; no leukocytes in field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows predominantly normocytic, normochromic red cells with occasional crenated forms. A small number of red cells, some with a faint polychromatic tint, contain coarse dark-blue punctate inclusions consistent with coarse basophilic stippling. Platelets appear adequate on this field, and no leukocytes are present for evaluation. The stippling is focal and only a few cells are affected in this field. Findings are consistent with coarse basophilic stippling, which in this clinical context supports lead toxicity; correlation with blood lead level is recommended.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are a small cluster of angular granules at the cell edge that are Prussian blue positive, unlike scattered iron-negative ribosomal stippling.
Thalassemia trait also shows stippling but with uniform microcytosis, hypochromia and target cells, and hemoglobin A2 is elevated.

ddx.dx: Fine basophilic stippling of polychromatic cells
ddx.vs: Fine stippling in reticulocytes is barely visible dust-like granularity, whereas lead causes coarse, distinct dots.
